text: Gaining an audience for your writing. <break time="0.8s" /> Involves not just finding a voice. <break time="0.8s" /> But ensuring that voice resonates. <break time="0.8s" /> With your intended readers. <break time="0.8s" /> Entrepreneurs understand the importance of building a brand. <break time="0.8s" /> That makes them memorable and distinct from their competitors. <break time="0.8s" /> Drawing customers to their products or services. <break time="0.8s" /> They achieve this. <break time="0.8s" /> By pinpointing their target audience. <break time="0.8s" /> Crafting a unique value proposition. <break time="0.8s" /> And shaping a recognizable identity. <break time="0.8s" /> While scholars might initially find these entrepreneurial concepts alien. <break time="0.8s" /> They actually engage in similar practices. <break time="0.8s" /> When they set themselves apart. <break time="0.8s" /> In their academic writing. <break time="0.8s" /> Consider the typical literature review and motivation section of a scholarly article. <break time="0.8s" /> The aim is to highlight gaps in existing research. <break time="0.8s" /> And position oneself as the one who will address these overlooked areas. <break time="0.8s" /> The challenge, as Labaree suggests. <break time="0.8s" /> Is not just in developing innovative ideas. <break time="0.8s" /> But in cultivating a distinctive voice. <break time="0.8s" /> That makes readers think, Ah, this sounds like the author. <break time="0.8s" /> It is about balancing the expression of your ideas. <break time="0.8s" /> With the development of a unique voice. <break time="0.8s" /> That leaves a lasting impression on your audience.
